anomalies.obs: On the Microcontroller sheet, the global labels are attached one pin low: CS0 sits on pin 18 (GPIO3/ADC1_CH3), SCK on pin 19 (GPIO4/ADC1_CH4), CS1 on pin 20 (GPIO5/ADC2_CH0), and CS2 on pin 21 (GPIO6), while SO is correctly on pin 16 (GPIO10). GPIO7 (pin 22) carries no label.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the SPI/CS lines are 'CS pins GPIO4/6/7' with 'SCK on GPIO5' and 'CS0/CS1/CS2, driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively', matching firmware constants (SPI2 on GPIO5, CS on GPIO4/6/7). anomalies.impact: The whole thermocouple SPI bus is wired to the wrong MCU pins: SCK is on GPIO4 instead of GPIO5, the three chip-selects are on GPIO3/GPIO4/GPIO5 instead of GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7, and GPIO7 is left unused. Firmware (which drives GPIO4/5/6/7/10) would never clock or select the MAX31855s correctly, so no valid temperatures are read; additionally GPIO3 is a boot-strapping pin now loaded by a thermocouple CS line.

anomalies.obs: On the Power sheet the +12V vertical rail is dotted onto both pin 1 and pin 2 of each fan header (J7 and J8); pin 4 of each is marked no-connect, and the only GND symbol in that column hangs at the bottom of the same +12V line. No fan header pin is tied to GND as a return.
anomalies.expected: The specification places only 'the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)' on the +12V net; by standard 4-pin fan practice pin 1 is the fan ground return, which must connect to GND, not to +12V.

anomalies.impact: The fans receive +12V on both power pins with no ground return, so neither fan spins and the open-collector tach signals (FAN_0_TACH/FAN_1_TACH) can never toggle, defeating the fan-stall fault detection; if the +12V rail and the GND symbol on that line are truly joined, it is a direct supply-to-ground short.
